name: Olympus Mons
description: Largest volcano in the solar system, standing over 21 km high with a caldera 80 km across.

name: Elysium Mons
description: Isolated volcanic peak rising 14 km above the lava plains of Elysium Planitia.

name: Ascraeus Mons
description: Northernmost of the three massive Tharsis Montes shield volcanoes, rising over 18 km.

name: Pavonis Mons
description: Central Tharsis volcano situated directly on the Martian equator.

name: Arsia Mons
description: Southernmost Tharsis volcano featuring a colossal 110 km wide summit caldera.

name: Alba Mons
description: Enormous low-relief volcanic construct covering an area roughly the size of the United States.

name: Hecates Tholus
description: Elysium volcanic dome showing evidence of explosive eruptions and glacial mantle deposits.

name: Jezero Crater
description: Ancient open-basin lake fed by Neretva Vallis; current exploration ground of NASA Perseverance rover.

name: Gale Crater
description: Features Mount Sharp (Aeolis Mons) rising 5 km from crater floor; NASA Curiosity rover site.

name: Gusev Crater
description: Ancient crater lake breached by Maadim Vallis; landing location of NASA Spirit rover.

name: Endeavour Crater
description: Meridiani Planum crater explored by the Opportunity rover for clay and sulfate minerals.

name: Korolev Crater
description: Northern polar crater permanently filled with a 1.8 km thick dome of pure water ice year-round.

name: Schiaparelli Crater
description: Prominent equatorial impact basin showing sedimentary layering and wind-eroded dunes.

name: Arandas Crater
description: Classic fluidized lobate ejecta blanket indicating impact into permafrost-rich substrate.

name: Bam Crater
description: Sharp-rimmed impact structure located near the Cydonia northern lowland dichotomy.

name: Calahorra
description: Prominent impact crater in western Chryse Planitia near the mouth of Simud Valles.

name: Grindavik
description: Crater in southern Chryse Planitia named after the Icelandic fishing town.

name: Alamos
description: Impact feature near the junction of Chryse outflow channels.

name: Cefalù
description: Well-defined crater rim in the Chryse Planitia alluvial delta zone.

name: Sefadu
description: Northern Chryse crater situated north of the Viking 1 landing zone.

name: Swanage
description: Crater situated along the Ares Vallis outflow path into Chryse basin.

name: Nakusp
description: Small crater in the primary traversal sector of ARES Nav EVA-1.

name: Belva Crater
description: Nested impact crater inside Jezero exposing cross-bedded river delta top deposits.

name: Chryse Planitia
description: Vast circular lowland plain where multiple giant flood channels emptied into an ancient sea.

name: Isidis Planitia
description: Major impact basin bordering Syrtis Major; host basin to Jezero Crater and Beagle 2.

name: Utopia Planitia
description: Largest recognized impact basin in the solar system; landing site of Viking 2 and Zhurong rover.

name: Hellas Planitia
description: Deepest impact basin on Mars, plunging over 7 km below datum with high atmospheric pressure.

name: Argyre Planitia
description: Second-largest impact basin in the southern highlands, surrounded by rugged mountain rings.

name: Acidalia Planitia
description: Expansive northern plains covered in dark basaltic sand dunes and putative submarine mud deposits.

name: Elysium Planitia
description: Smooth volcanic plain featuring young flood lavas; landing region of NASA InSight mission.

name: Valles Marineris
description: Massive canyon system stretching over 4,000 km, up to 200 km wide and 7 km deep.

name: Ares Vallis
description: Colossal catastrophic flood channel that carved teardrop islands into the Chryse plains.

name: Simud Valles
description: Braided mega-flood channel network named after the Sumerian word for Mars.

name: Tiu Valles
description: Major outflow valley converging into Chryse Planitia from the eastern Hydraotes chaos terrain.

name: Mawrth Vallis
description: Ancient valley system exposing thick strata of iron- and aluminum-rich smectite clays.

name: Kasei Valles
description: One of the largest outflow channel systems on Mars, cutting through Lunae Planum.

name: Melas Chasma
description: Deepest segment of Valles Marineris canyon, dropping 9 km below surrounding plateau.

name: Perseverance Landing Site (Octavia E. Butler)
description: Touchdown location of the Mars 2020 Perseverance rover and Ingenuity helicopter.

name: Curiosity Landing Site (Bradbury Landing)
description: Touchdown point of the Mars Science Laboratory (Curiosity rover) in Gale Crater.

name: Viking 1 Lander (Thomas Mutch Station)
description: First successful operational spacecraft to land on Mars; operated for over 6 years.

name: Viking 2 Lander (Gerald Soffen Station)
description: NASA lander in Utopia Planitia that performed primary biological soil analysis.

name: Mars Pathfinder (Carl Sagan Memorial Station)
description: First rover mission to Mars carrying the Sojourner microrover in Ares Vallis.

name: Opportunity Lander (Challenger Station)
description: Eagle Crater touchdown of Opportunity rover; verified past presence of liquid water.

name: Spirit Lander (Columbia Memorial Station)
description: Gusev Crater landing site of the Spirit Mars Exploration Rover.

name: InSight Lander Site
description: Elysium Planitia landing site of the geophysics lander that mapped Mars core and quakes.

name: Zhurong Rover Landing Site (Tianwen-1)
description: Southern Utopia Planitia landing site of China first operational Mars rover.

name: Cydonia Mensae
description: Dichotomy transition plateau featuring flat-topped mesas and famous orbital landmarks.

name: Face on Mars (Cydonia Butte B-1)
description: Eroded 2.5 km butte photographed by Viking 1; confirmed as natural feature by MGS.

name: D&M Pyramid
description: Geometrical pentagonal massif shaped by prolonged aeolian wind erosion in Cydonia.

name: Oxia Colles
description: Complex cluster of isolated low hills and mesas bordering Chryse Planitia and Ares Vallis.

name: Nili Fossae
description: Curved grabens northwest of Isidis Basin rich in olivine, clays, and carbonate mineral beds.

name: Arabia Terra
description: Heavily cratered Noachian crust; one of the oldest terrains preserved on Mars.
